subtopic: Repurchase Limits and Pro Rata Allocation
source_evidence: If shareholder requests for repurchase exceed the amount of outstanding shares eligible for repurchase during a repurchase offer, repurchase is generally done on a pro rata basis.
question: Misconception: If an interval fund receives more repurchase requests than it can fulfill, each shareholder is guaranteed to have all the shares they requested repurchased.
answer: That is not guaranteed. When requests exceed the shares eligible for repurchase, the fund generally allocates repurchases on a pro rata basis, so a shareholder may be able to sell only part of the shares they requested.
